Switching from Windows to Mac, users actually face very few software limitations. The platform can not only run all the most mainstream computer software, but also has countless practical applications that can only be used on Mac.

The only major exception is the gaming field. However, the latest tests show that Windows games run on Mac better than ever before, whether through official or unofficial means……

Apple provides a dedicated Game Porting Toolkit designed to help developers evaluate the performance of their Windows games on Mac, thereby encouraging and facilitating them to port games to the Mac platform.

However, according to Filipe Esposito of Macworld, this toolkit has also been used by players to unofficially run Windows software on Mac, and he himself is one of them. He said the latest test version has significant improvements in performance, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

After several days of testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta on the M4 Pro MacBook Pro, I found that the performance improvements fundamentally changed the experience of playing demanding Windows games……Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro equipped with 24GB of RAM, under the same game settings and benchmark conditions, the frame rate of GTA V jumped from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to about 176 fps on the GPTK 4 beta, an increase of about 66%. The game runs smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledged that not every game will see such dramatic results, but he hopes these improvements will encourage game developers to see Mac as a viable platform.
